name: FT-991A
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not a Yaesu publication and not affiliated with Yaesu.
verified: Compiled from the Yaesu FT-991A CAT Operation Reference Manual and Yaesu's published specifications, September 2026. The operating manual could not be read, so the panel keys and the operating procedures are absent from this card rather than guessed. Write yours in below.
specs: 30 kHz to 56 MHz, 118 to 164 MHz, 420 to 470 MHz
HF and 6 m, plus 2 m and 70 cm, amateur bands. Check your model's band edges
CW, AM, SSB, FM, RTTY, C4FM, and packet at 1200 and 9600 baud
5 to 100 W on HF and 6 m, 5 to 50 W on 2 m and 70 cm. AM carrier 2 to 25 W
23 A at 100 W, 15 A at 50 W on VHF and UHF
1.8 A with no signal, 2.2 A with one
Yes, automatic, with a hundred channel memory
USB for CAT and firmware, plus a separate GPS and CAT serial connector
filters: Narrow default 1.5 kHz, adjustable from 200 Hz to 1.8 kHz.
Narrow default 500 Hz, adjustable from 50 to 500 Hz.
Narrow default 300 Hz, adjustable from 50 to 500 Hz.
Narrow default 2.4 kHz, adjustable from 1.8 to 3.0 kHz.
500 Hz on the higher bands, with wider settings of 6, 9 and 16 kHz.
The narrow and wide touch key picks the mode-appropriate narrow filter. Touch the width key and rotate the multi knob to set the bandwidth.
control: Straight to the computer. The radio carries a USB to dual serial bridge, so one cable gives both CAT and the sound card ports
Yaesu's USB driver has to be installed first
The rear GPS and CAT connector, switched to serial by menu 028
4800, 9600, 19200 or 38400. Yaesu does not publish a default. Write yours below
notes: Twenty-three amps key down. A hundred watts from a portable supply is a short outing whatever the radio.
It has a real internal tuner, which is unusual in this class and worth knowing before you plan an antenna.
One cable does CAT and audio, which makes it the easiest of these radios to get onto digital modes and the easiest to key twice by accident.
The panel section of this card is empty on purpose. Yaesu's operating manual could not be read for it, and a guessed key sequence is worse than a blank line.
